text:
cheng: quick follow-up from the RFC sync — i want to propose a tiny change to how we marshal the safetensors-like header to enable cheaper per-shard validation and more granular warmup ops.

maria: curious — can you sketch the shape? i remember we landed on a compact header to save bytes.

cheng: yeah compact stays. idea is: split header into two logical sections — 'manifest' (static, global metadata) + 'shard index' (per-shard small records). include a lightweight 32-bit checksum per shard and a 64-bit container epoch. this lets loaders do a cheap checksum check before doing any mmap or crypto work.

raj: sgtm in principle. what's the failure/fallback path if checksum mismatch? full download?

cheng: plan: loader does these steps on open:
1) read global manifest (fast).
2) read shard index (small, fits in 4KB usually).
3) validate per-shard checksum against local cache tag. if pass -> mark shard as hot-ready without reading weights. if fail -> schedule granular warmup for that shard only.

olivia: so we avoid rehydrating whole bundle for one corrupt shard. nice. how do we surface partial failures to the serving runtime?

cheng: expose an enum from weights-loader: {OK, PARTIAL_DEGRADED, MISSING}. PARTIAL_DEGRADED includes list of shard ids flagged for warmup. serving runtime decides canary fallback (e.g., route to variant) or do synchronous warmup depending on policy.

maria: we need to be careful with security: checksum alone could be spoofed. do we rely on signed manifests elsewhere?

cheng: yes — container epoch + signature on the manifest. per-shard checksum only for integrity/perf gating. full trust still requires manifest signature verification (done by control plane on fetch).

raj: what about the cost/latency tradeoff for that extra index read? reading a 4KB index per start is fine but on cold VMs with cold disk it could still be a hop. any batching ideas?

cheng: loader will keep an in-memory ringcache of recent shard-indices keyed by model-version and storage-shard. we can also piggyback index reads into our existing manifest fetch flow so storage RPCs remain 1x.

olivia: warmup ops — you mentioned 'granular warmup'. sketch the operations/API so runtime can call them.

cheng: propose adding two RPCs to WarmupCoordinator: `probe_shard(shard_id)` -> returns quick metadata and `hydrate_shard(shard_id, priority)` -> async op that streams shard bytes and signals completion. both idempotent. warmup priority influences eviction leash and network priority.

maria: we already have a warmup queue but it's model-level. adding shard-level will need tweaking to autoscaler heuristics. not impossible.

raj: how do we reconcile with KV cache & prefix caching? if a shard is being hydrated for keys used in active requests, we want hydrate_shard to be high-priority and prebind the allocation.

cheng: agree — hydrate_shard should accept an optional `pin_for_request_id` token so the allocator reserves transient memory until request finishes or TTL expires. also we can emit traces so trace ids correlate warmup <-> request.

olivia: any compatibility story for older bundles lacking shard-index?

cheng: loader will detect missing index and fall back to legacy behavior (index-first or manifest-based read). we won't break old bundles. but new bundles will advertise `index_v2` in manifest and control plane will push conversion tools.

maria: testing plan? need microbenchmarks for index read cost, false positives, and recovery time when a shard fails checksum. also chaos test for partial-hydrate while serving.

raj: and update observability: add metrics: `shard_index_reads`, `shard_checksum_failures`, `hydrate_shard_latency`, and a per-model gauge `degraded_shards_count`.

cheng: yeah i'll open an RFC follow-up PR that includes:
- header layout example (proto-ish)
- loader state machine pseudocode
- warmup RPC surface and semantics
- backward compatibility notes
- simple perf microbench plan + dashboards

olivia: +1 to that. small nit: use 64-bit checksum for futureproofing? 32-bit might be fine but collisions could confuse heuristics.

cheng: leaning 32-bit for space, but we can make field variable-length and specify algorithm id. will call out in PR.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: reminder: checkin for loader changes must include migration plan for dedicated nodes and a rollout window.

maria: noted. i'll coordinate with infra and schedule a canary after RFC review.

raj: thanks cheng. lmk when PR lands and i'll run the cold-start bench harness. :thumbsup:

cheng: thanks all — PR incoming this afternoon.
